_comment: Tier-2 for skfem point_source#4, verified 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1. Claim: the integral of u over Omega equals a Green's-function balance and disagreeing with the analytic value by orders of magnitude signals a wrong source magnitude, wrong BC orientation or a sign error in K. The entry's stated identity ('-1/lambda1 in the Laplacian spectrum') is not right; the correct one is the double sine series sum over odd p,q of 16(-1)^((p-1)/2)(-1)^((q-1)/2)/(pi^4 p q (p^2+q^2)), summed here to p,q < 2001 giving 0.07367135. Ran: ElementTriP1 on MeshTri().refined(3..7), then three deliberate faults at r=6. Printed: the FE integral converges to the series at rates 1.978/1.994/1.999/2.000, reaching a 4.81e-05 relative gap, so the integral IS a usable verification quantity even though the pointwise solution is not. Doubling the source doubles the integral to 6 decimals; flipping the sign of K flips it exactly; dropping the Dirichlet condition on one side inflates it by 32%. All three are SILENT (empty warning list) -- so the entry's 'orders of magnitude' overstates the boundary case, which shifts by tens of percent and needs a tight tolerance to catch. MUTATION CONTROL (re-runnable): T2_MUTATE=1 undoes the three injected faults inside run() -- magnitude, sign and drop_one_side are forced back to 1.0, +1.0 and False, i.e. exactly the fixes the entry tells a user to make. Re-verified by execution 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1: the unmutated run matches all 7 expect_in_output strings; T2_MUTATE=1 makes all three fault runs identical to the healthy one, so the integral has nothing to catch and 'magnitude_error_is_caught=True', 'sign_error_is_caught=True' and 'bc_error_is_caught=True' disappear and the fixture goes red. Re-run: T2_MUTATE=1 python source.py
